overview: The Medford School Committee governs the city's public school district, overseeing educational policy, budgetary allocations, and facilities management. Meeting from September 2024 through October 2026, the body managed a significant leadership transition while navigating the complex multi-year planning process for a new comprehensive high school building. The committee oversaw the allocation of voter-approved override funds toward staffing and infrastructure and addressed district-wide capacity issues in elementary and after-school programs. At the conclusion of the record, the committee was focused on finalizing the district’s next strategic plan and refining policies for school reassignment and vocational admissions.

threads.name: Superintendent Search and Leadership Transition
threads.summary: Following the announced departure of Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent in early 2025, the committee moved to ensure leadership continuity during critical budget and facility cycles. Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi was appointed as Interim Superintendent in early 2025 and later received a formal induction and professional coaching framework. After a period of evaluation and public input regarding district leadership priorities, the committee voted in February 2026 to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent. This transition concluded with the approval of a three-year contract for Dr. Galusi in May 2026.

threads.name: Medford Comprehensive High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a multi-phase project with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) to replace or renovate the high school, selecting Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager. Throughout 2025 and 2026, the body finalized enrollment targets, refined an educational plan, and evaluated potential building sites while navigating complex property deed restrictions. Significant design decisions included prioritizing LEED Silver certification and net-zero energy goals while excluding dedicated community storage to preserve educational space. The project recently entered the schematic design phase with updated membership for the building committee.

threads.name: Infrastructure and HVAC Modernization
threads.summary: To address failing heating and cooling systems, the committee authorized 'construction management at risk' services for major HVAC replacements at the McGlynn and Andrews schools. A comprehensive facilities assessment in late 2025 identified over $80 million in priority repairs across five schools, leading to the approval of solar power purchase agreements and roof replacements. In 2026, the committee approved a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roofing at the Roberts Elementary School. The district continues to manage smaller capital needs including hot water heaters and security camera installations across multiple campuses.

threads.name: Curriculum, Graduation, and AI Policy
threads.summary: Following state changes to graduation mandates, the committee updated district policy to replace MCAS competency determinations with successful completion of aligned coursework. The body also adopted a comprehensive policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence, eventually prohibiting staff from using AI tools to grade qualitative student work. Other academic initiatives included the launch of a science-of-reading literacy plan and the implementation of honors pilots within the vocational program. Ongoing work involves aligning district standards with new statewide graduation framework recommendations.

threads.name: After-School Expansion and Restructuring
threads.summary: To address persistent waitlists, the committee commissioned a study from the Belmont Afterschool Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) to evaluate program capacity. Based on these recommendations, the district transitioned to a model featuring full-time site directors and increased capacity by 150 seats across the elementary schools. The committee also adjusted the program's rate card, introducing multi-day flexibility and a tiered fee structure to support expanded staffing. By late 2026, the administration reported a 68% reduction in the after-school program waitlist.

threads.name: Budgetary Strategy and Override Funding
threads.summary: The committee managed the allocation of voter-approved override funds, which were utilized to restore staff positions, fund vocational expansion, and build collective bargaining reserves. Financial planning included the navigation of a $5 million level-services gap in early 2026 and the reconciliation of capital funds following city budget adjustments. To manage unanticipated costs, the body established a special education reserve fund and regularly utilized budget transfers to address departmental overspending. The FY27 budget was finalized in June 2026 after identifying nearly $834,000 in additional deficit reductions.

threads.name: Enrollment and Space Utilization
threads.summary: Facing significant overcrowding at the Roberts Elementary School, the committee voted to relocate preschool classrooms to other buildings and added staffing to manage capacity. A broader proposal to restructure the district into different grade configurations was debated throughout 2025 but was ultimately delayed until 2028 to allow for better construction planning. The committee also reviewed student enrollment trends, which showed slight declines, and consistently voted to opt out of the state's school choice program to maintain space for local residents. Recent efforts have focused on formalizing a policy for alternative elementary school reassignments.

threads.name: Health, Safety, and Transportation
threads.summary: The district implemented remediation strategies for lead in water fixtures, eventually lowering its acceptable lead threshold and installing new filtration stations. Transportation safety became a focus in late 2025, leading to the use of paraprofessionals as bus monitors and a request for the city to adopt automated stop-arm enforcement cameras. The committee also updated policies regarding life-threatening allergies, bullying prevention, and student restraint protocols to align with state regulations. Late buses were introduced in late 2026 to expand access to after-school activities for high school students.
